clue.text: Law, say, is changed for good

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that legislation has been altered permanently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges LAW and SAY together; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: For good means permanently, forever, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Terrible fall sees trees like this

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A harsh autumn leaves the trees bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' is the American autumn, when trees lose their foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Trees after autumn have no foliage, bare of greenery.

indicators.note: inside places the cold letter within the warm word

parts.note: amiable means warm and friendly
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone polite and friendly on the outside, chilly within.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil means polite and friendly, a synonym.

clue.text: Get Iran upset with us endorsement

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Make Iran angry by getting our backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing a document is endorsing it, so the name written is an endorsement.

clue.text: Bottle up seeing journalists on drink

indicators.note: in an across clue, journalists on drink puts the journalists after the drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their feelings in check while watching reporters drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To bottle up feelings is to hold them down or conceal them, a synonym.

parts.note: a supporter seems to be a backer of Britain's National Health Service, but is literally one carrying a patient on a litter

explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical orderly who carries patients on a litter literally supports them.

indicators.note: includes means the landing holds the solitary word inside

parts.note: a pier is a landing stage
one means single, solitary

explanation.surface: A settler arrives alone at a landing place.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is an early settler, a kind of colonist.

indicators.note: containing means the rearranged letters hold the gold word
possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A rich place full of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' looks like the adjective rich, but 'possibly' makes it anagram fodder, giving ELDOADO for the gold to sit in.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold, a place of fabled wealth.

indicators.note: say indicates the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: surplus means extra, not needed

explanation.surface: A choirboy's robe is superfluous.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplice is a white liturgical vestment worn by choristers.

clue.text: Pretend to be ill? Stay with mum

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
to linger is to stay on

explanation.surface: A child fakes sickness so as to stay home with mother.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign sickness to avoid work is a dictionary sense of shirking duty.

indicators.note: after places the execute-plus-right pieces following the criminal

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
to do something is to execute it

explanation.surface: Kill a bird belonging to a crook, soon after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execute' suggests killing; it just means DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A large South American vulture, an example of the category.

clue.text: Fine end of April in rustic surroundings

indicators.note: the rustic forms surroundings round the letter in question

parts.note: a peasant is a rustic, a country person

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word April

explanation.surface: Weather report of a fine late April day in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of April' gives L, which goes inside PEASANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine weather is agreeable, nice, a synonym sense.

indicators.note: losing heart removes the central letter of the colour word

parts.note: neutral describes a pale, uncoloured shade

explanation.surface: Someone anxious goes white and loses courage.
explanation.walkthrough: NEUTRAL has seven letters, so 'losing heart' drops its middle T.
explanation.definitionFit: Neural means relating to nerves, the system of the body.

clue.text: Liberal queen taking anything for amusement

parts.note: aught is an old word for anything
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a queen

explanation.surface: A Liberal monarch will take anything to be entertained.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's standard queen; 'taking' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughter is the sound produced by amusement, a closely linked synonym.

clue.text: Tortuous English and American work finished

parts.note: labor is the American spelling of labour, work
ate means finished off a meal

explanation.surface: A complicated joint English and US project has been completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Complicated, intricate and involved, so twisting like a tortuous argument.

clue.text: 'I will shortly…', we hear, for Innisfree?

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: I will shortened is the contraction I'll

explanation.surface: A line apparently quoted from Yeats's poem about a lake retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeats's poem 'The Lake Isle of Innisfree' opens 'I will arise and go now'; the contraction I'll is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Innisfree is a small island in Lough Gill, an example of the category.

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a do is a party
later means following

explanation.surface: An admirer is one following a single party line.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, so is an excessive admirer.

clue.text: Look over an object of hatred

parts.note: lo is an old word for look
an is the indefinite article a
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Examining something one detests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link: in a down clue LO sits over the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense dislike or detestation is loathing, a synonym.

indicators.note: Initially takes the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: The hangman's tool shown at the start of an execution.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is the hangman's instrument of execution, so the cord is defined by its use.

indicators.note: fancy signals an imaginative rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: The lead actor of the cop show Dragnet, I suppose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' seems a film star; it is the astronomical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cool luminous body in space late in its life, an example of the category.

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
still means not moving, sedentary
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A secretary's office romance with a desk-bound partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small chewy confection, a kind of candy.
To drop is to lessen; to iron is to remove creases, punningly de-crease.

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
pens means shuts in, locks up

explanation.surface: Dredgers work on a river's locks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Wales, Scotland and England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dredging makes a channel go further down, which makes it lower.

indicators.note: before puts the coffee ahead of the next letter

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

indicators.note: mid picks the central letter of the word afternoon

explanation.surface: A second cup of coffee before mid-afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The latter of two is the second one mentioned.

indicators.note: unruly suggests letters behaving wildly and rearranged

explanation.surface: A badly behaved teenager gets a prison stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' rearranges TEEN and GAOL; 'stretch' looks like a prison term but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen is to stretch out, a synonym.

indicators.note: chasing puts the boss behind, following, the letter
middle picks the central letter of the word eastern

parts.note: a boss is a stud or rivet head

explanation.surface: A boss pursuing Middle Eastern backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle eastern' reads as the Middle East but gives T, the middle of EASTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A trivet is a three-legged stand that holds up a pot, a kind of stand.

clue.text: Interesting new leader admits a bad start

indicators.note: admits means the rearranged word lets the other letters inside
new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters
start picks the first letter of the word bad

explanation.surface: A new party leader concedes a poor beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges LEADER into READLE, which 'admits' A and B (start of bad).
explanation.definitionFit: An engaging book is easy and enjoyable to read, hence interesting.

clue.text: Sign on in Bognor Regis? Terrific

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Enrolling at the seaside town of Bognor Regis would be wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: Bognor Regis is a resort on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To register is to enrol, a synonym of signing on.

clue.text: Judge faces reversal on end of sentence

indicators.note: on sets the turned word next to that letter
end of picks the last letter of the word sentence
faces reversal means the word for faces is read backwards

parts.note: to face someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: A judge faces his verdict being overturned at the close of sentencing.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem is to regard or rate, so to judge someone highly.
